items.prompt: Black to move. Find the queen fork.

claims.statement: Qa1+ followed by Qxe5+ wins the knight.
Qa1+ is the engine's first choice.
No white piece covers a1, so the queen cannot be captured there.
Nothing defends the knight on e5.

hints: Look for a check that also attacks a second piece.
A queen on the first rank checks the king. What else does it attack along the long diagonal?
From a1 the queen sees the knight on e5.
items.explain: Qa1+ checks the king and attacks the knight on e5 along the diagonal. The king must deal with the check, and then the queen takes the knight. Nothing covers a1, and nothing defends e5.

feedback_by_move.a4c6: Trading queens wins nothing: the knight on e5 stays and Black has used up the only forcing move.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the pawn fork.

claims.statement: ...f4+ followed by ...fxg3 wins the rook for a pawn along the engine line.
...f4+ is the engine's first choice.

hints: Look for a check. A pawn can give one too.
A pawn attacks the two squares diagonally in front of it.
A pawn on f4 attacks e3 and g3. Which of your opponent's pieces stand there?
items.explain: ...f4+ attacks the king on e3 and the rook on g3 at the same time. The king must move, and the pawn takes the rook. A pawn is the cheapest piece to fork with, because no one wants to capture it with something valuable.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the queen fork.

claims.statement: Qb1+ followed by Qxc2 wins the rook.
Qb1+ is the engine's first choice.
No white piece covers b1.

hints: Look for a check.
The queen can check on the first rank and attack another piece in the same move.
Which white rook stands next to b1?
items.explain: Qb1+ checks the king and attacks the rook on c2. Nothing covers b1, so the queen cannot be captured, and the rook falls.

items.prompt: Black to move. The white rook now stands on c1 instead of c2. Does ...Qb1+ still win the rook? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: ...Qb1+ Rxb1 loses the queen.
The rook on c1 covers b1.

hints: The queen would land on b1. Who can capture on b1?
Can the target itself capture the forking piece?
items.explain: The rook on c1 stands next to b1, so after ...Qb1+ it simply takes the queen. A fork fails when the forking piece can be captured, even by one of its own targets.

items.prompt: Black to move. The white rook stands on d2. Does ...Qb1+ win material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: ...Qb1+ wins nothing along the engine line.
No white piece covers b1, but nothing is attacked from there either.

hints: After ...Qb1+, which white pieces does the queen attack besides the king?
items.explain: The check is safe, but the queen attacks no second piece from b1. A check is not a fork unless a second target stands on a line from the same square.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the knight fork.

claims.statement: Nd5 followed by Nxe7+ wins the bishop.
Nd5 is the engine's first choice.
Nothing defends the rook on c7.
The bishop on e7 is defended only by the rook on c7.

hints: Which two black pieces could one knight attack together?
A knight on d5 attacks c7 and e7.
Neither the rook nor the bishop is defended.
items.explain: Nd5 attacks the rook on c7 and the bishop on e7. The bishop is defended only by the rook, so once the rook moves away the knight takes the bishop with check.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's king stands on f8 and defends the bishop on e7. Does Nd5 still win a piece? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Nd5 only leads to a trade of knight for bishop along the engine line.
Two black pieces defend the bishop on e7: the rook and the king.

hints: Count the defenders of each target.
After the rook moves away and the knight takes the bishop, what recaptures?
items.explain: Black moves the rook away, and the king still defends the bishop. Nxe7 Kxe7 trades a knight for a bishop and gains nothing. The second target was defended, so taking it gained nothing.

items.prompt: White to move. Is there a tactic? If so, play it.

claims.statement: f4+ wins the rook along the engine line.
f4+ is the engine's first choice.

hints: Is there a check? A pawn can check too.
Look at the squares a pawn on f4 would attack.
A pawn on its starting square can move two squares.
items.explain: The pawn jumps from f2 to f4 with check, attacking the king on g5 and the rook on e5. It cannot be taken by anything, so the rook is lost.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a tactic that wins material?

claims.statement: Qa1+ followed by Qxe5+ gains nothing: a pawn recaptures.
The pawn on f4 defends the knight on e5.
The engine rates the position as roughly equal.

hints: Look for a check that attacks a second piece.
Then ask whether the queen could take that second piece safely.
items.explain: ...Qa1+ still attacks the knight, but now a pawn defends it, so taking it costs the queen. The check is not a winning fork.

items.prompt: Black to move. Which Black piece is pinned to its king? Tap it.

claims.statement: The bishop on e6 has no legal move.
The rook on e1 attacks the bishop along the open e-file.
The knight on f6, by contrast, can move.

hints: Which of your pieces stands between the white rook and your king?
If that piece stepped off the file, your king would be in check.
Look at the e-file.
items.explain: The bishop on e6 stands between the rook on e1 and the king on e8. If it left the e-file, the king would be in check, so no move by the bishop is legal. That is an absolute pin.

items.prompt: White to move. A Black piece is pinned. Win it.

claims.statement: f5 wins the bishop along the engine line.
f5 is the engine's first choice.
The rook on e1 pins the bishop to the king.

hints: Which black piece cannot move?
Attack the pinned piece with something it cannot run from.
A pawn is the cheapest attacker. Which pawn can reach a square attacking e6?
items.explain: The bishop on e6 is pinned, so it cannot step away. The pawn attacks it with f5, and even if the king unpins by moving, the bishop is still attacked, so White wins it.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's king now stands on d8, not e8. Does f5 still win the bishop? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: f5 wins nothing along the engine line.
The rook on e1 still attacks the bishop.

hints: Is there still a piece behind the bishop on the e-file?
Can the bishop move now?
items.explain: With the king on d8 there is nothing behind the bishop on the e-file. It is attacked, but it can simply move away, so f5 gains nothing. A pin needs something valuable behind the pinned piece.

items.prompt: White to move. The white rook stands on a1. Is any Black piece pinned? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: f5 wins nothing along the engine line.
No white piece attacks the bishop on e6.

hints: Which white piece attacks along the e-file now?
items.explain: Nothing attacks the bishop on e6, so nothing is pinned. A pin needs an attacker aiming along the line.

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight on f6 is pinned to the queen, not the king. Tap every square the knight can legally move to.

claims.statement: The knight has six legal moves.
The bishop on g5 attacks the knight.
The queen is not attacked directly: the knight shields it.

hints: Is your king behind the knight on that line?
If the queen, not the king, is behind the knight, are knight moves still legal?
items.explain: The queen, not the king, stands behind the knight, so the pin is relative: every normal knight move is legal. Whether it is wise is a separate question.

items.prompt: Black to move. The pinned knight can legally move. If Black plays ...Nd7, does Black lose material? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: ...Nd7 Bxd8 loses the queen for a bishop along the engine line.
The queen is shielded by the knight right now.

hints: What does the bishop on g5 attack once the knight has gone?
Compare the value of the queen with the value of the bishop.
items.explain: Once the knight leaves, the bishop on g5 attacks the queen on d8 and takes it. The move was legal but loses the queen for a bishop. 'Cannot move' (absolute pin) and 'should not move' (relative pin) are different.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a tactic? If so, play it.

claims.statement: ...f4 wins a bishop for a pawn at least along the engine line.
...f4 is the engine's first choice.

hints: Which white pieces cannot move freely?
A piece in front of its king on a line the enemy rook controls cannot leave it.
Which pawn can attack the pinned piece?
items.explain: The rook on e8 pins the white bishop on e3 to the king on e1. The pawn attacks the bishop, which cannot step away, so Black wins it.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a tactic that wins material?

claims.statement: ...f4 wins nothing along the engine line.
The engine rates the position as roughly equal.

hints: Is any white piece shielding something valuable on a line?
What happens if the attacked bishop just moves?
items.explain: The white king is no longer behind the bishop on the e-file, so the bishop is not pinned. It can move away from the pawn, and ...f4 wins nothing.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the skewer.

claims.statement: Bd6+ followed by Bxa3 wins the rook.
Bd6+ is the engine's first choice.
Two white pieces cover d6: the bishop itself and the rook on d1, which defends it after Bd6+.

hints: Look for a check along a diagonal.
A skewer attacks the king first. What stands on the same diagonal behind the king?
The bishop checks on d6; the rook on a3 is on the same diagonal.
items.explain: Bd6+ checks the king on c5, and the rook on a3 stands on the same diagonal behind it. The king must move out of the check, and the bishop takes the rook. The rook on d1 defends the bishop, so the king cannot take it.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the skewer.

claims.statement: Qa2+ followed by Qxg8 wins the queen.
Qa2+ is the engine's first choice.
Nothing defends the queen on g8.

hints: Look for a check on the long diagonal.
Which white piece stands on the same diagonal behind the king?
The queen on a2 checks along a2-g8.
items.explain: Qa2+ checks the king on c4, and the white queen on g8 stands on the same diagonal behind it. The king moves, and the queen takes the queen. Nothing defends the queen on g8.

items.prompt: White to move. The white rook is on g1 instead of d1, so nothing defends d6. Does Bd6+ still win the rook? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bd6+ Kxd6 loses the bishop.
Only the bishop itself covers d6: the rook on g1 does not defend it.
The king attacks d6.

hints: The bishop lands next to the king. Can the king capture it?
Does anything defend the square d6?
items.explain: The king stands next to d6 and simply takes the undefended bishop. A skewer fails when the front piece can capture the attacker.

items.prompt: White to move. The black king stands on b5. Does Bd6 skewer anything? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bd6 wins nothing along the engine line.
The bishop and the rook cover d6, but Bd6 gives no check.

hints: Is the black king on the diagonal of the bishop on d6?
items.explain: With the king on b5 the diagonal d6-a3 has no king on it, so Bd6 is no check and forces nothing. The rook can simply move.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a tactic? If so, play it.

claims.statement: ...Rd5+ followed by ...Rxd1 wins a rook.
...Rd5+ is the engine's first choice.

hints: Is there a check that also lines up another piece?
Look along the d-file and the fifth rank.
The rook checks on d5; what stands on the d-file behind the king?
items.explain: ...Rd5+ checks the king on d3 along the d-file, and the white rook on d1 stands behind it on the same file. The king steps aside and ...Rxd1 wins the rook.

items.prompt: Black to move. Is there a tactic that wins material?

claims.statement: Qa2+ followed by Qxg8 Rxg8 only trades queens along the engine line.
The rook on g5 defends the queen on g8.
The engine rates the position as roughly equal.

hints: Is there a check that lines up another piece?
If the piece behind is taken, can it be recaptured?
items.explain: Qa2+ still lines up the queen on g8 behind the king, but now the rook on g5 defends it. Queen takes queen, rook takes queen: an even trade, not a win.
